## Endpoints

### Data Read (1)
- `GET /{id}` — Get details about a specific agent by its ID.

### Data Write (1)
- `POST /v1/projects/aiagentstore/installations` — Install the agent in a project.

### Media (1)
- `GET /sounds/notification.mp3` — Download a notification sound.

### Realtime (2)
- `GET /google.firestore.v1.firestore/listen/channel` — Listen for real-time updates from Firestore.
- `POST /google.firestore.v1.firestore/listen/channel` — Send data to Firestore via a real-time channel.

### Config (1)
- `GET /{id}/projects/-/apps/1:622990908402:web:3d0f646f757564cf2f696b/webconfig` — Retrieve the web configuration for a specific app.

### Core API (1)
- `GET /claw/open` — Open the claw (likely for robotic agents).

## Quick Start

### OpenClaw (Unbrowse) workflow
- Authenticate in the browser first (no credentials are shipped with this skill).
- Capture fresh auth locally: run `unbrowse_capture` on an authenticated page for this domain.
- Execute via backend gate + client browser executor: `unbrowse_replay` with `executionMode="backend"`.

Example:
```text
unbrowse_replay { service: "aiagentstore", executionMode: "backend", endpoint: "GET /{id}" }
```

Here are some quick examples to get you started interacting with the `aiagentstore` API:

```typescript
// Get details about a specific agent by its ID.
async function getAgentDetails(agentId: string) {
  try {
    const agent = await client.getAgent(agentId);
    console.log("Agent Details:", agent);
    return agent;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Error fetching agent details:", error);
    return null;
  }
}
```

```typescript
// Install an agent in a project.
async function installAgent(projectId: string, agentConfig: any) {
  try {
    const installationResult = await client.installAgent(projectId, agentConfig);
    console.log("Agent Installation Result:", installationResult);
    return installationResult;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Error installing agent:", error);
    return null;
  }
}
```
